title: Bridge and Uniform
premise: In the river town of Vellsmark, on the eve of the Weavers' Revolution, Bram Okafor works as a typeface cutter in her late father's print shop, where the guild ledger holds every name, debt, and secret of the district. When the royal army requisitions the town and seizes the ledger to build its case against the printers' conspiracy, Bram discovers her own family's name among those marked for the gallows. She steals the ledger and must carry it past three army checkpoints to the smuggler's ship departing on the morning tide — but each checkpoint costs her something: an ally arrested, a lie exposed, a piece of her old self burned away. At the final gate she is recognized by Captain Ilse Verren, the officer who once sheltered her as a child; instead of arresting her, Ilse tears her own commission in half and walks Bram through, choosing justice outside the law. The ship sails with the evidence, the revolution's trials collapse for lack of proof, and Bram — orphaned by the fire that covers her escape — finds a new found family among the smugglers and typesetters who sail with her.
about_author: Orsen Amberdale is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring antique printing equipment in coastal mill towns before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for meticulous craft detail and stories of ordinary people caught in the gears of history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Bram Okafor cuts typefaces in her father's print shop, measuring her world in what can be carried — a font tray, a grudge, a memory. POV: Bram. Establishes her precision, her grief for her father, and the town's restless mood. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Master Quill, the shop's owner, shows Bram the guild ledger — every printer, debtor, and sympathizer in Vellsmark recorded in her father's hand. She learns her father secretly kept names off the list to protect people. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: awe at her father's hidden mercy, first hint the ledger is dangerous.

chapters.title: Red Coats at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Army scouts cross the river bridge and post proclamation: the town will be requisitioned at week's end. The printers' guild meets in secret; Quill argues the ledger must be destroyed, others say hidden. POV: Bram observing from the doorway. Emotional beat: dread arriving like weather.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Bram packs the shop against seizure, teaching her young apprentice Tally what matters and what can burn. She hides a duplicate set of type matrices under the floorboards. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: tenderness toward Tally, foreshadowing the theme of carrying versus leaving.

chapters.title: The Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers occupy Vellsmark; the print shop is sealed as 'evidence.' Captain Ilse Verren oversees the inventory and pauses at Bram's name on the tenancy papers — recognition flickers. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: violation, and the unsettling sense of being seen.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Knew Her
chapters.summary: Verren summons Bram privately, revealing she once lodged with the Okafor family during a famine winter and owes them a debt. She warns Bram not to interfere with the investigation. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: complicated gratitude tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Ledger Vanishes
chapters.summary: Overnight the guild ledger disappears from the sealed evidence room. The army blames the printers; Quill swears he didn't take it. Bram realizes whoever has it controls every life in the district. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: panic sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tally's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tally saw a clerk named Doss carry a wrapped bundle to the garrison — the ledger kept alive as leverage, not destroyed. Bram understands: names will be traded for confessions. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the stakes become personal when she spots her own surname on a posted warrant draft.

chapters.title: Marked for the Gallows
chapters.summary: A leaked list shows eleven names slated for trial, including Okafor and Quill. The guild scatters; some beg Bram to flee. She refuses — running means the ledger stands as truth. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Offer
chapters.summary: Bram seeks out Nessa Kade, a river smuggler who owed her father printing debts. Kade agrees to carry the ledger out on the morning tide in three days — if Bram brings it aboard herself. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fragile hope with a hard price.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Kade maps the route: the market gate, the bridge checkpoint, the harbor quay. Each is searched differently; each demands a different disguise or lie. POV: Bram planning. Emotional beat: the comfort of a plan, and the knowledge plans fail.

chapters.title: Quill's Confession
chapters.summary: Quill admits he informed on the guild years ago under torture, and his testimony anchors the case. He begs Bram to let him surrender and buy time. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fury, then pity — justice is murkier than she believed.

chapters.title: First Gate: The Market
chapters.summary: Disguised as a laundress, Bram passes the market gate by trading gossip with the sergeant's wife — information as currency. Inside, she cases the garrison records room. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into terror when she sees Doss again.

chapters.title: Doss's Price
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Doss, offering him forged discharge papers in exchange for access to the evidence room. He wavers — he hates the army more than he loves it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance built on mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: Night in the Records Room
chapters.summary: With Doss's key, Bram reaches the evidence vault but finds the ledger gone again — moved to Verren's personal quarters. Someone inside the army is protecting it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: despair, then a terrible realization about who her ally really is.

chapters.title: The Second Copy
chapters.summary: Bram discovers her father anticipated this: a partial second ledger hidden in the type matrices under the floorboards — names in code only a typeface cutter could read. It proves the conspiracy but not the army's thefts. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: her father reaching across death to help her.

chapters.title: Tally Taken
chapters.summary: The army arrests Tally on suspicion of theft, intending to sweat a confession out of a child. Bram's deadline now carries a hostage. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: guilt like a stone in the chest; the mission doubles.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Verren
chapters.summary: Bram trades the coded ledger's existence for Tally's release — lying that it's already aboard the ship. Verren lets the girl go but orders the harbor searched at dawn. POV: alternating Bram and Verren. Emotional beat: two women circling each other, both hiding mercy.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns
chapters.summary: Frightened guild members denounce Bram to save themselves, revealing her route to the authorities. The market gate is now closed to her. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: betrayal by her own community; belonging revealed as conditional.

chapters.title: Kade's Doubt
chapters.summary: Nessa Kade considers cutting losses and sailing without Bram. A night of honest talk about debts, fathers, and the sea renews their pact — but Kade won't wait past the tide. POV: Kade. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Second Gate: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Bram attempts the bridge disguised as a corpse-tender hauling a plague coffin — the ledger sealed inside beneath a real body. The sergeant demands the coffin opened. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the book's most sustained suspense; she talks her way through by seconds.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Held
chapters.summary: Past the bridge, Bram opens the coffin to retrieve the ledger and finds the dead man wears a guild pin — Quill, dead by his own hand, leaving a confession naming Doss's handler. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief and rage braided together; the evidence grows heavier.

chapters.title: Ilse's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV shift: Verren reads the stolen guild ledger alone at night, finding her own name recorded among officers paid to look away during the famine. She understands why the army wants it buried. Emotional beat: her loyalty cracks along an old wound.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashe, Doss's handler, is revealed as the architect — he stole the ledger to purge rivals and protect himself, letting printers hang as cover. POV: Bram learning this from Quill's confession. Emotional beat: the enemy has a face, and it outranks everyone.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Shop
chapters.summary: Ashe burns the print shop to destroy the hidden matrices. Bram watches her childhood go up in smoke and salvages one thing: her father's cutting knife. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: total loss distilled into a single held object.

chapters.title: Refuge Among Strangers
chapters.summary: Hunted, Bram shelters with the smugglers' crew — a cook, a boy rigger, a defector soldier — who feed her without questions. For one evening she belongs somewhere. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: warmth as fuel for the last push.

chapters.title: Doss's Choice
chapters.summary: Ashe discovers Doss's treachery. Doss flees to Bram, bringing the original ledger's location: Ashe's private strongbox aboard the requisitioned customs sloop. POV: Doss. Emotional beat: a coward finally spending his courage.

chapters.title: Third Gate: The Harbor Quay
chapters.summary: The quay is locked down for dawn searches. Bram's plan: get aboard the customs sloop during the officer's changeover, take the ledger, and cross the water to Kade's ship. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: no more disguises left — only nerve.

chapters.title: Aboard the Sloop
chapters.summary: Bram and Doss slip aboard at night. She cracks the strongbox using her type-cutter's knife and lifts the ledger — but Ashe's adjutant raises the alarm mid-theft. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: triumph interrupted by alarm bells.

chapters.title: Run Across the Water
chapters.summary: Chased along the docks, Bram sends Doss ahead with the ledger while she draws the soldiers off. She is cornered at the pier's end as the tide turns. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely, at last understanding her father.

chapters.title: Verren at the Pier
chapters.summary: Verren arrives with soldiers — and orders them to search the wrong warehouse, buying Bram minutes. Alone with Bram at the pier's end, she asks why she should burn her career for a stranger's daughter. POV: Bram and Verren. Emotional beat: the debt of the famine winter comes due.

chapters.title: The Torn Commission
chapters.summary: Verren remembers the Okafors feeding her when the army let her starve on garrison rations. She tears her commission in half, walks Bram past the last sentries under her own authority, and stays behind to face arrest. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the climax's emotional peak — justice chosen over law, at cost.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Bram reaches Kade's ship as the anchor rises. The ledger, Quill's confession, and Doss's testimony go into the hold. Behind them, Vellsmark wakes to smoke and empty piers. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: escape without victory yet — the race becomes a voyage.

chapters.title: Ashe's Pursuit
chapters.summary: Ashe commandeers a fast cutter and pursues downriver, determined to sink the evidence rather than face trial. POV: alternating Ashe and Kade. Emotional beat: the net closing over open water.

chapters.title: The Fight at the Narrows
chapters.summary: At the river narrows, Kade runs the shallows Ashe's cutter cannot, aided by the boy rigger's local knowledge. Shots are exchanged; Doss is wounded shielding the ledger. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the found family fighting as one body.

chapters.title: Deliverance
chapters.summary: They reach the estuary and hand the ledger to the revolutionaries' council waiting aboard a neutral merchantman. The evidence is copied and scattered beyond any army's reach. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: relief so large it feels like grief ending.

chapters.title: The Trials Collapse
chapters.summary: Weeks later, word arrives: with the ledger published in pamphlets printed from Bram's surviving matrices, Ashe's case disintegrates; he is arrested by his own side. The condemned walk free. POV: Bram reading news sheets — printed on her type. Emotional beat: her craft literally sets the record straight.

chapters.title: What Verren Paid
chapters.summary: Verren faces court-martial; Bram returns secretly to testify on her behalf, tipping the scales to demotion instead of hanging. The two meet once more, evenly, as equals. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: debts acknowledged, forgiveness neither simple nor complete.

chapters.title: A New Press
chapters.summary: Bram, Tally, Doss, and Kade's crew establish a floating press aboard Kade's ship, printing truth up and down the coast. Belonging, Bram learns, is something you build and carry, not something you're given. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet joy, hard-won.

chapters.title: The First Impression
chapters.summary: The maiden run of the floating press: Bram sets the first line herself — her father's motto, 'Measure the world in what can be carried' — and pulls the lever. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: resolution and beginning at once; the story ends as the ink dries.
